# Set up Crosshead for Claude Code

<!-- Generated by scripts/host-plugins.mjs; do not edit. -->

Crosshead shares one local runtime across projects and hosts. Start by asking
where the user wants automatic memory. Recommend the current project. Offer
additional directories, all projects, or manual commands only. Confirm the
profile for each directory; reuse an existing profile when the user selects
one. Explain that source excerpts can preserve exact workspace text and reach
the hosted service and later model prompts. Enable excerpts only on request.

1. Check `crosshead --help` and `crosshead workspace list --json`. If the CLI is
   missing or its help lacks `--scope`, explain the install and ask for explicit
   consent before running `curl -fsSL https://crosshead.sh/install | bash`.
   The installer verifies the downloaded release digest and installs the
   runtime. A new hosted profile uses a local key and authenticates to its
   selected service. When Crosshead is installed, reuse its runtime home.
2. Preview the user's selection. Replace the example profile name with the
   user's choice. Add `--api-base https://crosshead.sh` only if they want to
   create a new hosted profile.

   ```sh
   crosshead quickstart --scope project --adapter claude-code --workspace-root . --profile WORK --dry-run --json
   ```

   Use `--scope all` for user-wide hooks or `--scope manual` for manual use.
   Show the paths, profiles, source excerpt choices and any replaced hooks.
   Apply the confirmed command without `--dry-run`. For further directories
   with existing profiles, preview and apply `crosshead workspace add`.
3. Open a fresh session in the selected project.
   Run `crosshead workspace check --json`. Report the configured profile and
   whether startup or resume has been observed. Check an unselected directory
   when the user chose project scope.

Use `crosshead workspace remove` to detach a project. Keep machine-specific
hook entries local. Use an explicit `--profile` for memory commands when
working outside a configured project.
